name: i2c
description: Pi 4 bare-metal I2C bus service on BSC1 (GPIO 2 SDA / GPIO 3 SCL, 100 kHz, PIO). Not a device driver: the hub and the language model reach any device on the bus through SREQ ops 1 scan, 2 read(addr, reg, n), 3 write(addr, bytes) — the tool with which an unknown device gets incubated. Same address on the QEMU twin (i2c-bus.1), where virtual devices can be plugged in with -device.

hardware.controller: BCM2711 BSC1 at 0xFE804000 (BSC0 0xFE205000 and BSC2 0xFE805000 are the other two)
hardware.pins: GPIO 2 (SDA1) / GPIO 3 (SCL1): the resident sets ALT0 + pull-up itself at INIT (GPFSEL0, GPIO_PUP_PDN_CNTRL_REG0)
hardware.clock: DIV 1500 from the 150 MHz core clock = 100 kHz
hardware.twin: QEMU raspi4b: i2c-bus.0/1/2 = BSC0/1/2; tmp105, lsm303dlhc_mag, ds1338, pca9552 models work; at24c-eeprom crashes QEMU when probed

lessons: a bus scan is a 1-byte read per address (zero-length transfers never finish on QEMU's model)
QEMU's BSC model begins a transfer on ANY C write with I2CEN set, so write C exactly once per transfer, after A and DLEN
write data goes into the FIFO after the transfer is active (TA), reads drain the FIFO while RXD — this order suits the silicon too
ERR (no ACK) comes without DONE on the model; break on ERR

mappings.what: GPIO: GPFSEL0 / pull control for GPIO 2-3

process: EL0 unit in SLOT_RESIDENT; the BSC1 window is its only capability.
